# Ultima III on the New 3DS

This is the MS-DOS Ultima III: Exodus with the Exodus Project upgrade (VGA graphics and music), running in DOSBox with a front end built for the 3DS's two screens.

The game is on the top screen at its true shape (4:3, full height). The strips on either side show information the game makes you dig for. The bottom screen is your keyboard, map, notebook and library.

# Starting a new game

When the title appears, press Space (X button, or Pass on the command pad). Then use the letters on the command pad:

- O - Organize a Party
- C - Create a Character, then fill in a number (1-20), name, sex, race, type and attributes
- F - Form a Party from up to four characters
- M - back to the Main Menu
- J - Journey Onward to begin

The Book of Play explains races, types and attributes. A balanced first party is a fighter, a cleric, a wizard and a thief or paladin.

# Buttons

These work the same way in every 3DS port:

- D-pad or circle pad - move (the arrow keys). Hold to keep walking; let go and the party stops at once.
- A - Enter
- B - Esc (cancel)
- X - Space (pass a turn, skip)
- Y - open or close the keyboard
- ZL or SELECT - swap the two screens (see below)
- ZR - fast-forward (hold it; can be switched to a toggle in Settings)
- L / R - previous / next bottom-screen tab (in a book: previous / next section)
- START - the menu: Resume, Manual, Save game, Settings and Exit game. B or START closes it.

A and B can be swapped in Settings.

Left-handed play (Settings): the D-Pad and the A, B, X and Y buttons swap places (Y and Up, A and Right, B and Down, X and Left). It applies everywhere, including this manual, and is remembered.

Presses are never stored up. If the game is still busy with your last press, a new one is ignored rather than played later, so the party never runs on by itself. When the game takes a moment to answer, a small "Working..." bar appears at the top of the game screen; "Saving..." means files are being written to the SD card.

# Swapping the screens

Press ZL (or SELECT) at any time to put the game on the touchscreen, where it fills the whole screen. The tabs then move to the top screen, between the info strips:

- D-pad - move the highlight between the buttons on the top screen; A presses the highlighted button
- Circle pad - move the party
- Tap the map on the touchscreen to take one step toward where you tapped
- L / R still change tabs, and START still opens the menu

Press ZL again to put everything back. "Game on the touchscreen" in Settings does the same, and it is remembered.

# The Commands tab

Every Ultima III command is one letter. The pad shows all 26 with their names. Tap one to press that key. Commands that usually matter where you are now are tinted gold: Klimb and Descend in a dungeon, Transact in a town, and so on.

The bottom row has 1-4 for choosing a party member (the bars under the names are their health), 0-9 for amounts, and Spells for the spell list.

Most commands ask a follow-up question at the bottom of the game screen, such as a direction or a number. When the game asks for a direction, the bottom row turns into North, South, West and East buttons; when it asks yes or no, it shows Yes and No. You can also answer with the D-pad or the pad's buttons. Buttons that can't be used right now (such as an empty party slot) are greyed out and do nothing.

Ultima III has no conversation typing: walk up to someone and use T (Transact) with a direction.

# Typing

Two commands take a typed word: O (Other) and Y (Yell). Tapping either one opens the keyboard by itself.

The gold buttons across the top of the keyboard are words you'll want to type. They come from clues you pinned on the Log tab and from words you typed before. Tap a word, then Enter.

The keyboard also opens with Y, the Abc button, or 0-9 (numbers first).

# Info strips (top screen)

Left strip:

- Moons - the phases of Trammel (silver) and Felucca (gold), 0 to 7, as the game counts them
- Wind - the direction the wind is blowing while you're outdoors (it matters when sailing). The name is where it blows from.
- Party - one bar per character: green is healthy, yellow is hurt, red is in danger, purple is poisoned, gray with a slash is dead
- Food - the lowest food count in the party. It turns orange below 100 and flashes red below 50.

Right strip:

- Marks and Cards - eight slots that stay blank until someone in the party carries that item
- In a dungeon: the level you're on and which way you face

Turn the strips off in Settings if you want plain black bars.

# The Map tab

The map draws itself as you explore. Nothing appears until you've seen it.

- Outdoors and in towns: the land around you fills in as you travel. Zoom in shows real tile art; drag to look around and tap Center to follow the party again. Whole shows the entire map.
- In dungeons: each level is drawn from what the party could see down the corridors, with doors, ladders (blue arrows), chests, fountains and writings. Traps and other hidden things are never shown. Use the 1-8 buttons to look at other levels. A gold dot marks the level you're on.
- Places lists every town, castle and dungeon you've explored, so you can review it any time.

The map is saved on the SD card. If you start a brand-new game, use Reset auto-map in Settings.

# The Log tab

Everything the game prints in its message window is collected here, so nothing scrolls away. Drag to scroll.

Tap a line to pin it as a clue. Pinned lines are kept for good with the place you heard them. Pinned only shows just your clues. Words from pinned clues show up as buttons on the keyboard.

# The Book tab

- This guide
- Spell list - every spell, what it does and what it costs
- Reference card - all 26 commands, A to Z, and their 3DS buttons
- Book of Play - the original manual as large, readable text. See page jumps to that page of the original.
- The original pages - the Book of Play, both spellbooks and the cloth map, with zoom
- Cluebook - only listed if you turn it on in Settings, because it gives answers away

Reading works the same way as in every other 3DS port:

- Circle Pad or C-Stick - scroll (hold to keep scrolling; on page scans, move around the page)
- D-Pad - move between the section buttons on the left; A opens the one you picked
- L / R - previous / next section (on page scans, the previous / next page)
- Tap a section to open it; drag the text or page to move it
- B or START - close the book and go back to where you were
- Page scans: + and - (or X and Y) zoom in and out

While a book is open, nothing you press reaches the game. Books goes back to the list of books.

The original manuals are not included with this program. The setup script makes them from your own GOG copy of Ultima III.

# Saving

The game saves when you use Q (Quit) while outdoors, or Save game in the START menu (which does the same thing, and is greyed out anywhere else). Do that before you stop playing. The next time you start, choose Journey Onward to continue.

To leave, use Exit game in the START menu. It asks first, because anything since your last save is lost.

Closing the 3DS lid puts everything to sleep. Your map, clues and settings are saved when you leave the program, and when the 3DS sleeps.

# A few spoiler-free tips

- Buy food early and keep an eye on the Food number.
- Look (L) before stepping into unfamiliar terrain.
- In dungeons, light a torch with I (Ignite).
- Talk to everyone with T (Transact), and pin anything that sounds important.
- Chests are often trapped. A thief, or the cleric spell Appar Unem, can disarm them.
